Present perfect: I have been.explain_en: We use the present perfect for experiences in our life, when the exact time is not important: “I have been to London.” “Have you ever eaten sushi?”
Present perfect: I have been.explain_ar: بنستخدم المضارع التام للتجارب في حياتنا لما الوقت بالظبط مش مهم: “I have been to London.”

examples.en: I have never seen snow.
Have you ever met a famous person?

check.question: Which sentence is about a life experience?
check.why_ar: التجربة من غير وقت محدد بالمضارع التام.

Present perfect: I have been.explain_en: Make it with have or has + the past participle: play → played, go → gone, see → seen, eat → eaten. He, she and it take “has”.
Present perfect: I have been.explain_ar: بنكوّنه بـ have أو has + التصريف التالت: played وgone وseen وeaten. ومع he وshe وit بنستخدم has.
Present perfect: I have been.board:
I / you / we / they have + done
he / she / it has + done

examples.en: She has finished her homework.
We have lived here for five years.
examples.ar: إحنا ساكنين هنا من خمس سنين.

check.question: He ___ visited Japan twice.
check.why_ar: مع he بنستخدم has.

Present perfect: I have been.explain_en: If you say WHEN (yesterday, in 2020, last week), use the past simple: “I saw it yesterday”, not “I have seen it yesterday”. No time or up to now → present perfect.
Present perfect: I have been.explain_ar: لو قلت إمتى (yesterday أو in 2020) استخدم الماضي البسيط. ولو مفيش وقت أو لحد دلوقتي → المضارع التام.
Present perfect: I have been.board: finished time → past simple · up to now → present perfect

examples.en: I lost my keys yesterday.
I have lost my keys! (I can’t find them now)

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I have seen him last week.
I have saw him last week.
check.why_ar: last week وقت محدد خلص، فالماضي البسيط.

Present perfect: I have been.explain_en: Use for + a period (for two years) and since + a start point (since 2020). “Just” = a moment ago, “already” = earlier than expected, “yet” in questions and negatives.
Present perfect: I have been.explain_ar: for مع مدة (for two years)، وsince مع بداية (since 2020). just = من شوية، وalready = خلاص بدري، وyet في السؤال والنفي.
Present perfect: I have been.board: for 3 years · since Monday · just · already · yet

examples.en: I’ve known her since primary school.
Have you finished yet? — Yes, I’ve just finished.

check.question: I have studied English ___ 2021.
check.why_ar: 2021 نقطة بداية، فبنستخدم since.

Present perfect: I have been.recap_en: Use have or has with the past participle for experiences and for things connected to now. If you say when it happened, use the past simple instead.

First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_en: We use the first conditional for real things that may happen in the future and their result: “If it rains, we will stay at home.”
First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_ar: بنستخدم الشرط الأول لحاجات ممكن تحصل فعلاً في المستقبل ونتيجتها: “If it rains, we will stay at home.”

examples.en: If you study, you will pass.
If I see Ali, I’ll tell him.

check.question: Which is a real future possibility?
options: If it rains tomorrow, we’ll stay in.
If I were a bird, I’d fly.
If I had known, I’d have come.
check.why_ar: المطر بكرة حاجة ممكن تحصل فعلاً.

First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_en: Use if + present simple, then will + verb. The present comes after “if”, even though we mean the future.
First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_ar: if + مضارع بسيط، وبعدين will + الفعل. بعد if بنستخدم المضارع حتى لو قصدنا المستقبل.

examples.en: If she calls, I will answer.
We’ll miss the bus if we don’t hurry.

check.question: If you ___ hard, you will improve.
check.why_ar: بعد if بنستخدم المضارع البسيط.

First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_en: Arabic speakers often say “If it will rain…”. In English, never use will after if in this structure: “If it rains”, not “If it will rain”.
First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_ar: غلطة مشهورة: “If it will rain”. ماينفعش will بعد if هنا: “If it rains”.
First conditional: If it rains, ….board: If it rains ✓ · If it will rain ✗

examples.en: If I have time, I’ll call you.
If he comes late, we’ll start without him.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: If he will come, I will be happy.
If he comes, I will be happy.
check.why_ar: بعد if مضارع (comes) من غير will.

First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_en: “Unless” means “if not”: “You won’t pass unless you study.” We use the first conditional for warnings, promises and advice.
First conditional: If it rains, ….explain_ar: unless معناها if not: “You won’t pass unless you study.” وبنستخدم الشرط الأول في التحذير والوعد والنصيحة.

examples.en: Unless you hurry, you’ll be late.
If you touch that, you’ll get hurt!

check.question: “You won’t get better ___ you rest.”
check.why_ar: unless = لو ما … (if not).

First conditional: If it rains, ….recap_en: Use if + present simple with will + verb for real future possibilities. Never put will after if, and remember unless means if not.

Past continuous: I was reading.explain_en: We use the past continuous for an action that was in progress at a moment in the past: “At 8 o’clock I was reading.”
Past continuous: I was reading.explain_ar: بنستخدم الماضي المستمر لحاجة كانت شغالة في لحظة في الماضي: “At 8 o’clock I was reading.”
Past continuous: I was reading.board: at that moment in the past

examples.en: Yesterday at 6 pm we were playing football.
It was raining all morning.

check.question: Which means “كنت بتعشى الساعة ٨”?
check.why_ar: حاجة كانت شغالة في لحظة → was having.

Past continuous: I was reading.explain_en: Use was with I, he, she, it and were with you, we, they, + verb-ing: “They were watching TV.”
Past continuous: I was reading.explain_ar: was مع I وhe وshe وit، وwere مع you وwe وthey، وبعدها الفعل + ing.
Past continuous: I was reading.board:
I / he / she / it was + -ing
you / we / they were + -ing

examples.en: She was cooking when I arrived.
We were waiting for you!

check.question: They ___ sleeping when the phone rang.
check.why_ar: they مع were.

Past continuous: I was reading.explain_en: Use the past continuous for the long action and the past simple for the short action that interrupts it: “I was walking home when it started to rain.”
Past continuous: I was reading.explain_ar: الماضي المستمر للحدث الطويل، والماضي البسيط للحدث القصير اللي قاطعه: “I was walking home when it started to rain.”
Past continuous: I was reading.board: long action (was -ing) + when + short action (past simple)

examples.en: I was taking a shower when the doorbell rang.
examples.ar: كنت باخد دش لما الجرس رن.

examples.en: While we were driving, we saw an accident.

check.question: I ___ TV when my friend called.
check.why_ar: الفرجة كانت شغالة (طويلة)، والمكالمة قاطعتها.

Past continuous: I was reading.explain_en: Use “while” with the long action and “when” with the short one. For two long actions at the same time, use while + past continuous twice.
Past continuous: I was reading.explain_ar: while مع الحدث الطويل، وwhen مع القصير. ولو حدثين طوال في نفس الوقت: while + ماضي مستمر للاتنين.

examples.en: While I was studying, my brother was playing games.
When the lights went out, we were eating.

check.question: ___ I was cooking, the cat jumped on the table.
check.why_ar: with the long action (كنت بطبخ) نستخدم While.

Past continuous: I was reading.recap_en: Use was or were with verb-ing for actions in progress in the past, and the past simple for a short action that interrupts them.

will or going to?.explain_en: English has two common ways to talk about the future: “will” and “going to”. They are both correct, but we choose by meaning.
will or going to?.explain_ar: في طريقتين مشهورين للمستقبل: will وgoing to. الاتنين صح، لكن بنختار حسب المعنى.

examples.en: I’ll help you.
I’m going to start a new course.

check.question: Both will and going to talk about …
check.why_ar: الاتنين للمستقبل، والفرق في المعنى.

will or going to?.explain_en: Use will for decisions you make at the moment of speaking, and for promises and offers: “The phone’s ringing — I’ll get it!”
will or going to?.explain_ar: will للقرار اللي بتاخده وقت الكلام، وللوعود والعروض: “The phone’s ringing — I’ll get it!”

examples.en: I’ll call you tonight, I promise.
That bag looks heavy. I’ll carry it.

check.question: “It’s cold.” — “OK, I ___ close the window.”
check.why_ar: قرار اتاخد في لحظة الكلام → will.

will or going to?.explain_en: Use going to for plans you made before, and for predictions with clear evidence now: “I’m going to visit my aunt on Friday.” “Look out! You’re going to fall.”
will or going to?.explain_ar: going to لخطة متقررة قبل كده، أو لتوقع عليه دليل قدامك: “Look out! You’re going to fall.”
will or going to?.board: plan made before · I can see it → going to

examples.en: We’re going to paint the kitchen this weekend.
She’s going to have a baby.

check.question: I bought paint yesterday. I ___ paint my room.
check.why_ar: خطة متقررة قبل كده (اشتريت الدهان) → going to.

will or going to?.explain_en: For predictions based on opinion, we often use will with “I think”, “probably” or “I’m sure”: “I think it will be a great match.”
will or going to?.explain_ar: للتوقعات اللي مبنية على رأي بنستخدم will مع I think أو probably: “I think it will be a great match.”
will or going to?.board: I think … will · probably · I’m sure

examples.en: I’m sure you’ll love Alexandria.
It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

check.question: “I think Egypt ___ win the match.”
check.why_ar: توقع مبني على رأي مع I think → will.

will or going to?.recap_en: Use will for quick decisions, promises, offers and opinions about the future. Use going to for plans you already made and for things you can see coming.

should / must / have to.explain_en: Use “should” to give advice or say what is a good idea: “You should drink more water.” The negative is “shouldn’t”.
should / must / have to.explain_ar: should للنصيحة أو الحاجة اللي يستحسن تتعمل: “You should drink more water.” والنفي shouldn’t.

examples.en: You should see a doctor.
You shouldn’t stay up so late.

check.question: Your friend has a headache. You say:
check.why_ar: نصيحة → should + الفعل في أصله.

should / must / have to.step_title: must and have to: strong obligation
should / must / have to.explain_en: Use “must” and “have to” for things that are necessary. “Must” often comes from the speaker; “have to” is often a rule from outside: “I have to wear a uniform at school.”
should / must / have to.explain_ar: must وhave to للحاجات الضرورية. must غالباً من رأي المتكلم، وhave to غالباً قانون من برا: “I have to wear a uniform.”
should / must / have to.board: must + verb · have / has to + verb

examples.en: I must remember her birthday.
She has to work on Saturdays.

check.question: He ___ wake up at 6 for work.
check.why_ar: مع he بنقول has to.

should / must / have to.explain_en: Careful! “Mustn’t” means it is not allowed. “Don’t have to” means it is not necessary — you can choose: “You mustn’t smoke here.” “You don’t have to come.”
should / must / have to.explain_ar: خلي بالك! mustn’t = ممنوع. وdon’t have to = مش ضروري، براحتك.
should / must / have to.board: mustn’t = ممنوع · don’t have to = مش لازم

examples.en: You mustn’t use your phone in the exam.
You don’t have to bring food. We have lunch.
examples.ar: مش لازم تجيب أكل، عندنا غدا.

check.question: Tomorrow is a holiday. We ___ go to school.
check.why_ar: إجازة يعني مش ضروري نروح، مش ممنوع.

should / must / have to.explain_en: After should and must, use the base verb with no “to”: “You must go”, not “You must to go”. Only “have to” has “to”.
should / must / have to.explain_ar: بعد should وmust الفعل في أصله من غير to: “You must go”. الوحيدة اللي فيها to هي have to.
should / must / have to.board: should / must + verb · have to + verb

examples.en: We should leave now.
I had to finish early yesterday.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: بعد must الفعل في أصله من غير to.

should / must / have to.recap_en: Use should for advice, and must or have to for strong obligation. Mustn’t means not allowed, but don’t have to means not necessary.

who / which / that.explain_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun, so we can join two sentences: “I have a friend. She lives in Dubai.” → “I have a friend who lives in Dubai.”
who / which / that.explain_ar: الجمل الموصولة بتزود معلومة عن اسم، فبنقدر نوصل جملتين: “I have a friend who lives in Dubai.”
who / which / that.board: noun + who / which / that + extra information

examples.en: The man who called you is my uncle.
This is the phone which I bought.

check.question: Which joins the sentences correctly?
options: I know a girl she speaks French.
I know a girl who speaks French.
I know a girl which speaks French.
check.why_ar: للأشخاص بنستخدم who.

who / which / that.step_title: who for people, which for things
who / which / that.explain_en: Use “who” for people and “which” for things and animals. “That” can be used for both in everyday English.
who / which / that.explain_ar: who للأشخاص، وwhich للحاجات والحيوانات. وthat تنفع للاتنين في الكلام العادي.
who / which / that.board: people → who · things → which · both → that

examples.en: The teacher who helped me was kind.
The book that I’m reading is great.

check.question: The film ___ we watched was scary.
check.why_ar: film حاجة مش شخص، فبنستخدم which (أو that).

who / which / that.explain_en: Arabic says “الكتاب اللي قريته” with “ه”, but in English we don’t repeat it: “the book which I read”, not “the book which I read it”.
who / which / that.explain_ar: بالعربي بنقول “قريته” بالهاء، لكن بالإنجليزي ما بنكررش الضمير: “the book which I read” مش “I read it”.
who / which / that.board: the book which I read ✓ · … I read it ✗

examples.en: The cake that my mum made was delicious.
examples.ar: الكيكة اللي ماما عملتها كانت لذيذة.

examples.en: The city which we visited is very old.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: The car which I bought it is red.
The car which I bought is red.
The car who I bought is red.
check.why_ar: ما بنكررش it بعد الفعل.

who / which / that.explain_en: Use “where” for places (the café where we met) and “whose” for possession (the boy whose bike was stolen).
who / which / that.explain_ar: where للأماكن (the café where we met)، وwhose للملكية (the boy whose bike was stolen).

examples.en: That’s the hospital where I was born.
I met a woman whose son is a pilot.

check.question: This is the school ___ I studied.
check.why_ar: school مكان، فبنستخدم where.

who / which / that.recap_en: Use who for people, which for things, that for both, where for places and whose for possession — and don’t repeat the pronoun at the end.
